clue.text: Assume performance banning women's ruled out

indicators.note: banning says the letter for women is kept out of the word for performance

parts.note: a show is a performance
W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of ruled are put out of order

explanation.surface: A show that has excluded women is ruled out of bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning' removes W from SHOW, leaving SHO; 'out' rearranges RULED into ULDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden or responsibility is to take it on, to assume it.

clue.text: Long grass totally pointless

indicators.note: pointless here means losing compass points, and totally means both of them, south and north

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, to snitch

explanation.surface: A lawn of long grass with no point to it at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb here. The compass points S and N are both stripped from SNITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to long for it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Close with a lot of property?

definitions.meaning: jokingly, someone full of stuff, possessions, is stuff-y

explanation.surface: A house nearby surrounded by lots of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room is close, lacking fresh air; the second reading treats the word as stuff plus an adjective ending.

clue.text: Silly bugger whose next-but-one successor was worse

definitions.text: Silly bugger whose next-but-one successor was worse

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of the following words are muddled up

explanation.surface: An insult for a fool whose successor-but-one proved still worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' rearranges BUGGER WHOSE. The whole clue is the definition: Obama followed the 43rd US president, then Trump, the 'worse' one.
explanation.definitionFit: The 43rd US president was widely mocked as foolish, and Donald Trump came two presidents after him.

clue.text: Recognise why attack's mounted after head of state loses face

indicators.note: after says the reversed pieces follow the trimmed head of state
losing its face means the word drops its front letter

parts.note: Joe Biden, US president when the puzzle appeared

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: why sounds like the letter Y
a fit is an attack of illness or temper

explanation.surface: Recognising why a fit has been staged after a disgraced leader's humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of state is Joe Biden, US president when the puzzle appeared in 2021; 'loses face' drops his initial, and 'mounted' reads the why-attack pair upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify someone is to recognise who they are, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Eagerness to get at mince pie's deplorable

indicators.note: deplorable implies something badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone so eager for a mince pie that it is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is AT MINCE PIE; the 's is read as 'is', a link, and 'deplorable' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is restless eagerness for something to happen now.

clue.text: Horrified by experiences in a high-speed car

indicators.note: in puts the word for experiences inside the car letters

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a fast touring car
has, as in has a hard time, means experiences

explanation.surface: Terrified by what happens riding in a fast car.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast describes being shocked and filled with horror.

clue.text: Wage that shamed liberal's how much?

indicators.note: liberal suggests a free treatment, so these letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking the cost of a pay deal that embarrassed a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' looks like a politician but is the anagram signal for WAGE THAT SHAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial question asks the price or bill, just as how much does.

clue.text: See 8
See 4
Escaped across back of yard with nothing much

indicators.note: with joins the slang word for nothing to the front

parts.note: FA, as in sweet FA, is British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: across says the escape word stretches around the extra letter

parts.note: to run away is to escape

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone fled over the end of the yard with very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escaped' looks like the definition but supplies wordplay; 'much' alone defines. Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Far and away is an intensifier meaning by far, very much, as in far and away the best.

clue.text: Having headless torso outside, Nancy's said: 'This isn't normal!'

indicators.note: outside puts the trimmed body round the French word
headless means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: the torso is the body
Nancy is a French city, and dit is French for said

explanation.surface: A grotesque body without a head, and someone called Nancy remarking that it is abnormal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a woman's name but is the city in eastern France, so what is said there is French.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is something strange, a thing departing from what is normal.

clue.text: Home schooling to start — little ones very amused

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: to start means only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: a titch is British slang for a small person, so titches are little ones

explanation.surface: Home schooling the youngsters to begin with, the children laughing a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes S from schooling. TITCH is British informal for a tiny person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in stitches means laughing hard, the idiom for being highly amused.

clue.text: Quarter settled first on scones, not wafers (they want the cream on top)

definitions.text: they want the cream on top

parts.note: E, east, is one quarter of the compass
lit means alighted, settled
1st, written IST, is first

indicators.note: not means the wafers are taken away from the scones

parts.note: taken as written
ice cream cones are wafers

explanation.surface: A cream tea debate: scones first, never wafers, with cream on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes CONES (ice-cream wafers) from SCONES, leaving S. The cream is the social elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitists believe the best people, the social cream, should be in charge.

clue.text: Hurried past Coventry's original ground

indicators.note: past says the word for hurried comes after the letter from Coventry
original means the opening letter only

parts.note: hurried means rushed

explanation.surface: Someone hurried past Coventry's first football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' gives C from Coventry, which 'past' places before RUSHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground here is the past participle of grind, so crushed is a synonym.

clue.text: Issue about old lady who doesn't live here now

indicators.note: about puts the word for issue round the grandmother

parts.note: to issue is to emit
gran, grandmother, is an old lady

explanation.surface: A dispute about an elderly woman who has moved away.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant is someone who has left their country to settle abroad.

clue.text: No old money coming back hurt country

indicators.note: coming back means the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
to mar is to damage or hurt

explanation.surface: A country hurt as no money returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns NAY + M into MYAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Myanmar is the Southeast Asian country formerly called Burma.

clue.text: A lecherous host welcomed in glamorous hangers-on

indicators.note: welcomed in means the host is taken inside the lustful word

parts.note: randy means lustful, lecherous
MC, master of ceremonies, is a host

explanation.surface: A lecherous host lets glamorous followers in.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm candy is slang for an attractive companion worn on the arm as decoration.

clue.text: Called round on policeman's orders

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the policeman goes below
round means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: named means called
DS, detective sergeant, is a policeman

explanation.surface: Called round to receive a police officer's instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: DS, detective sergeant, is a British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands are firm requests, commands, so orders in the noun sense.

clue.text: Supporter of PM once getting mouthful over lie

indicators.note: over means the mouthful is spread over the lair

parts.note: a bite is a mouthful
an animal's lie is its lair

explanation.surface: A follower of a former prime minister telling a big lie.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was the UK prime minister from 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: A Blairite is a follower of former British PM Tony Blair.

clue.text: Nothing between left and right — feasible view?

indicators.note: between places the zero between the two letters for left and right

parts.note: OK means all right
O is the round shape of zero, nothing
on, as in that is not on, means possible, feasible

explanation.surface: A neutral centrist view between political left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: To look on is to watch or view as a spectator.

clue.text: Fantasies about mothers overwhelming

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so the mothers surround the word for about

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Fantasies about overbearing mothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreams are fantasies, imaginings of what one wishes for.

clue.text: She doesn't admit getting small promotion

indicators.note: promotion moves the letter up, earlier in the down entry

parts.note: to deny is not to admit, so denies

explanation.surface: A woman who won't confess to getting a minor promotion at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' lifts S above I in DENIES, giving the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Denise is a female first name, so she is a woman called that.

clue.text: Pressure drops over time, definitely

parts.note: force is pressure

indicators.note: over means the rain falls over the letter for time, enclosing it

parts.note: raindrops make rain

explanation.surface: Pressure is certainly dropping over time.
explanation.definitionFit: For certain is an idiom meaning surely, without doubt.

clue.text: Robbery not entirely legal, burglar reflected

indicators.note: reflected says the hidden letters are read backwards
not entirely says only part of these words is used, hiding the answer in them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A robbery is partly legal, the burglar reflects.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'not entirely' in the definition; it is the hidden-word signal, and 'Robbery' alone defines BLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Blag is British slang for a robbery, especially a violent one.

clue.text: Fight roughly after losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: about means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: A rough brawl after someone was beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a boxing or wrestling contest, a fight.

clue.text: Run about in empty garden

indicators.note: in puts the word for about inside
empty means the word is emptied of its middle, leaving the outside letters

parts.note: over can mean about, as in fuss over

explanation.surface: Running about in a bare garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a country or firm is to govern it, to manage it.

clue.text: Put off date — notice children around

indicators.note: around means the children go round the notice

parts.note: issue means offspring, children
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: A meeting postponed when notice of children is given.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissuade someone is to put them off doing something.
